source: While there does appear to be a small increase in births from June to July, that seems to be a consistent yearly trend in Suffolk County.
claim: In Suffolk County, NY, births rose from 1,313 in June 2013 to 1,426 in July 2013.
code: d.assign(C=lambda x: x.County.fillna(0).astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(5)).assign(S=lambda x: x.C.str[:2]).query("C == '36103' and Year == 2013 and Month in [6, 7]").set_index('Month').countyBirths

source: In fact, if we look only at June and July births, we'll see that 2013 falls in the middle of a period of low births in the area, with no apparent baby boom in sight.
claim: June-plus-July births in Suffolk County, NY, totaled 2,739 in 2013, the second-lowest of the 21 years; only 2012, with 2,735, was lower.
code: d.assign(C=lambda x: x.County.fillna(0).astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(5)).assign(S=lambda x: x.C.str[:2]).query("C == '36103' and 1995 <= Year <= 2015 and Month in [6, 7]").groupby('Year').countyBirths.sum().sort_values().head(3)

source: And in this case, July of 2005 (just about 9 months after the win) saw the fewest summer Boston babies of all 21 years.
claim: July 2005 had 757 births in Suffolk County, MA (Boston), the fewest of any July from 1995 to 2015.
code: d.assign(C=lambda x: x.County.fillna(0).astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(5)).assign(S=lambda x: x.C.str[:2]).query("C == '25025' and 1995 <= Year <= 2015 and Month == 7").groupby('Year').countyBirths.sum().sort_values().head(3)

source: Nine months after the attack, Oklahoma City was looking at their lowest number of January births in all 21 years.
claim: January 1996 had 771 births in Oklahoma County, OK, the fewest January births of the 21 years from 1995 to 2015.
code: d.assign(C=lambda x: x.County.fillna(0).astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(5)).assign(S=lambda x: x.C.str[:2]).query("C == '40109' and 1995 <= Year <= 2015 and Month == 1").groupby('Year').countyBirths.sum().sort_values().head(3)

source: However, annual births in the city have declined about 30% since 1995, suggesting that economic turmoil may have a more long-term effect.
claim: Wayne County, MI, recorded 32,915 births in 1995, falling to 23,488 in 2015.
code: d.assign(C=lambda x: x.County.fillna(0).astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(5)).assign(S=lambda x: x.C.str[:2]).query("C == '26163' and Year in [1995, 2015]").groupby('Year').countyBirths.sum()

source: Every year, the Sunshine State sees its biggest spike in births in the late summer and early fall.
claim: Across 1995-2015, Florida's median monthly births are highest in September (18,934), October (18,911) and August (18,867).
code: d.assign(C=lambda x: x.County.fillna(0).astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(5)).assign(S=lambda x: x.C.str[:2]).query("S == '12' and 1995 <= Year <= 2015").drop_duplicates(subset=['Year', 'Month']).pivot_table(index='Year', columns='Month', values='stateBirths').median().sort_values(ascending=False).head(3)

source: That spring time dip virtually disappears, with birth counts remaining relatively consistent throughout the spring and summer.
claim: In Maine, each month from March through August accounts for between 8.37% and 8.91% of the 1995-2015 total.
code: d.assign(C=lambda x: x.County.fillna(0).astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(5)).assign(S=lambda x: x.C.str[:2]).query("S == '23' and 1995 <= Year <= 2015").drop_duplicates(subset=['Year', 'Month']).groupby('Month').stateBirths.sum().pipe(lambda s: (s / s.sum() * 100).round(2))

source: The pattern of few spring time babies and lots of late-summer babies is common in the southern states, but is less pronounced in the northern states.
claim: Over 1995-2015, spring (March-May) accounts for 24.00% of Florida's births but 25.63% of Maine's.
code: d.assign(C=lambda x: x.County.fillna(0).astype(int).astype(str).str.zfill(5)).assign(S=lambda x: x.C.str[:2]).query("S in ['12', '23'] and 1995 <= Year <= 2015").drop_duplicates(subset=['S', 'Year', 'Month']).assign(Season=lambda x: x.Month.map({1: 'Winter', 2: 'Winter', 3: 'Spring', 4: 'Spring', 5: 'Spring', 6: 'Summer', 7: 'Summer', 8: 'Summer', 9: 'Fall', 10: 'Fall', 11: 'Fall', 12: 'Winter'})).groupby(['S', 'Season']).stateBirths.sum().unstack().pipe(lambda t: t.div(t.sum(axis=1), axis=0) * 100).round(2)

source: You'll notice that all 10 regions see an increase in births in the summer months, but beyond the summer season, the number of births differs between northern and southern regions.
claim: In all ten Standard Federal Regions, summer (June-August) has the largest share of annual births, from 25.73% in Region 4 to 26.42% in Region 1.

source: In the springtime, more northern babies are born, while southern babies are born in larger numbers in the fall.
claim: Spring's share of annual births is highest in the northern Regions 8 (25.62%), 10 (25.58%) and 1 (25.43%) and lowest in the southern Regions 6 (23.96%) and 4 (24.19%), while fall's share is highest in the southern Regions 6 (25.73%), 9 (25.61%) and 4 (25.52%).
